result: `GET /health` now runs a real database round trip on every probe. I added `app/Http/Controllers/HealthController.ts`, which registers the framework's `DatabaseCheck` (named `db`, `critical: true`, 2s timeout) on a `HealthManager` and adapts the ORM's Drizzle handle from `config/database.ts` into the `query(sql)` connection the check expects — the handle is resolved per request, so a database that cannot be opened, whose `SELECT 1` throws, or that hangs past the timeout all surface as a failed check rather than a cached flag; the raw-SQL call picks `all`/`execute`/`run` off the handle so the probe survives a driver swap. `routes/web.ts` now points `GET /health` at that controller (named `health`, still unauthenticated and still covered by the existing host-authorization exemption in `src/app.ts`), and the controller answers `200` with `{ status: "healthy", timestamp, checks: [{ name: "db", status: "healthy", message, duration }] }` or `503` with `status: "unhealthy"` and the same per-check breakdown when the database check fails. `tests/HealthController.test.ts` covers the healthy path, a 503 with `status`/`checks[db].status` of `unhealthy` when `getDatabase()` throws (patched via `mock.module` behind a flag so other suites keep a real connection), and recovery afterwards; regenerated `.guren/routes.gen.ts` and `.guren/api-client.gen.ts` are included. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (5 tests across 3 files) both pass, and `bunx guren check` reports 0 failures.
